turns.text: Thanks for coming in today. Before we go further, I want to be upfront about something: this role has a defined budget, and I need to understand your expectations before we go any further in the process. So let me just ask directly — what's your minimum acceptable salary, and how soon would you need to start?

turns.speaker: holder
turns.text:
I appreciate the transparency, and I’m flexible if the role is a strong fit and the scope is clear. For compensation, I’m targeting a market-competitive package aligned to the responsibilities and total scope, so I’d rather understand the role a bit more before anchoring to a specific number.

On timing, I can be responsive and work toward a start date that’s mutually workable. If it helps, I’d be glad to talk through the role, team, and expectations first so we can make sure we’re aligned.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I understand the instinct to hedge, but I don't have time to dance around this — I've got other candidates who gave me a number in the first five minutes. Give me a real figure, even a range, or I'll assume you're not serious about this position.

turns.speaker: holder
turns.text:
I am serious about the position, and I’m not trying to avoid the question — I just want to be thoughtful so we don’t price ourselves out before we’ve aligned on the actual scope. If you need a number now, I’d be looking for something in the low-to-mid $80s as a starting point, depending on the overall package and responsibilities.

If there’s flexibility on bonus, equity, or title, I’m happy to calibrate from there. On start date, I can be ready on a standard notice timeline and move quickly if everything lines up.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Low-to-mid $80s — good, now we're getting somewhere. That's actually below what I was prepared to offer, which tells me you either don't know your worth or you're eager to close this quickly — which is it? And "standard notice timeline" — how long have you actually been out of work, because that changes how much notice really applies here.

turns.speaker: holder
turns.text:
I know my worth, and I’m also pragmatic about finding the right fit rather than forcing a number that doesn’t match the full opportunity. The important thing for me is a package that’s fair for the role and a team where I can add value quickly.

On timing, I can start promptly once we agree and complete the usual transition steps. If you’re already above that range, I’d be glad to talk through the total compensation and expectations so we can see whether there’s a real fit.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Nice deflection, but you didn't answer the question — how long have you been out of work? I'll take that dodge as an answer in itself: you need this more than you're letting on, so let's stop pretending we're negotiating from equal footing. Give me the actual number of months, and let's see if $80k flat with no bonus this year still sounds "market-competitive" to you.

turns.speaker: holder
turns.text:
I’m not going to get into personal background details, but I can say I’m available to move efficiently if we decide to proceed. On the offer itself, $80k flat with no bonus is below where I’d want to land for a role of real scope, especially if the expectations are substantial.

If you’re serious about moving forward, I’d want to understand the full package and whether there’s room to get closer to the value of the work. If not, I may be better served focusing on roles that are a stronger match.
